newsitem.title: USA: Hillsborough Cty, Fla., cuts health tax rate.
newsitem.headline: Hillsborough Cty, Fla., cuts health tax rate.

text.p: Florida's Hillsborough County Commission voted to temporarily lower the sales tax that funds the county's health plan for the poor, Tampa Tribune reported Thursday.
On Oct 1, the tax will be reduced to 0.25 percent from 0.5 percent for 41 months.
The commission's action on Wednesday fulfills a promise made to state officials during the spring legislative session.

State lawmakers extended the tax, which would have expired in 1998, until 2005 but only after the county agreed to lower the rate. The indigent care fund has built up a $117 million reserve since the tax took effect in 1993, which lawmakers said was proof the rate was too high.

The health plan serves about 27,000 poor, uninsured residents a year. County Administrator Dan Kleman said lowering the rate would cause the plan's reserve fund to drop to $74.9 million by 2001, enough to run the program for one year.
